voices.note: the mishna at 83a.6-8 (four occasions of the year)
anonymous redactorial voice; raises והא לא משך at 83a.11 and cites R' Yochanan at 83a.14

props.gloss_en: on these four occasions [one compels the butcher to slaughter], therefore if [the ox] died, it died to the buyer
but on the rest of the days of the year it is not so; therefore if it died, it died to the seller
R' Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak: the mishna in fact speaks of one who did not pull, where [the seller] transferred it to him through another
on these four occasions, where it is a benefit to him, one may act in a person's interest in his absence
on the rest of the days of the year, where it is a detriment to him, one may not act to a person's detriment in his absence
on these four occasions the Sages set their words upon Torah law
R' Yochanan: by Torah law, money acquires
and why did they say pulling acquires? a decree, lest he say to him: your wheat was burned in the loft

supports.gloss_en: דאמר רבי יוחנן: דבר תורה מעות קונות, and pulling is only a decree lest he say 'your wheat burned in the loft'

objections.gloss_en: והא לא משך -- but the buyer never pulled the animal; how is it his loss?

answered_by.gloss_en: לעולם שלא משך, וכגון שזיכה לו על ידי אחר -- on these occasions it is his benefit, and זכין לאדם שלא בפניו (= p_zikah_al_yedei_acher, p_zachin_leadam_shelo_befanav)
R' Elazar in R' Yochanan's name: on these four occasions the Sages set their words upon Torah law (= p_heemidu_al_din_torah)
